question: What is a major ethical debate surrounding Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) like IVF?

options.A: Guaranteed elimination of all genetic diseases at birth
options.B: Compulsory fertility treatment for all citizens
options.C: Fair access and what to do with unused embryos
options.D: Total absence of any legal regulations worldwide

explanation: ART often raises tough questions about fairness in who can afford it and how leftover embryos should be handled ethically. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h6)

question: Why does the trigone area of the bladder stay smooth instead of forming folds when empty?

options.A: It lacks any mucous membrane lining completely.
options.B: It is made of rigid bone-like cartilage tissue.
options.C: Its mucous membrane is firmly attached to the muscle layer.
options.D: It stays permanently stretched by constant fluid pressure.

explanation: You nailed it! While the rest of the bladder wrinkles up (forming rugae) when empty, the trigone is tightly anchored down so it stays nice and smooth. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T3#GNS121_U2_T3_h2)

question: Why might a patient's stool or urine test show a false negative early in a schistosomiasis infection?

options.A: The eggs dissolve immediately in fresh urine or stool samples.
options.B: The parasites hide inside bone marrow where tests cannot reach.
options.C: Eosinophils in the blood destroy all eggs before they reach excretory organs.
options.D: Adult worms have not yet matured and begun laying eggs.

explanation: Tests look for eggs. If the infection is brand new, the worms are still growing up and haven't started laying eggs yet! Always good to keep repeat testing in mind. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T10#GNS214_U1_T10_h5)

question: Why do researchers often recruit more people than their minimum calculated sample size?

options.A: To increase the chance of getting statistically insignificant results
options.B: To account for participants who drop out or withdraw during the study
options.C: To satisfy hospital administrators who love large group numbers
options.D: To make the data entry process longer for student assistants

explanation: Exactly! People travel, fall ill, or change their minds. Adding a buffer upfront saves your project if participants drop out. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T18#GNS224_U1_T18_h5)

question: In which year was the historic Alma-Ata Declaration on Primary Health Care held?
explanation: The landmark international conference that shaped modern community nursing took place in Alma-Ata in 1978. Great to keep in mind for your exams! [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h2)

question: What is a major drawback of relying only on traditional lectures in nursing training?

options.A: It takes too much time to cover basic medical definitions
options.B: It prevents the instructor from using any visual aids like slides
options.C: It can leave students passive and rarely tests their practical clinical skills
options.D: It requires every student to have a private computer in the hall

explanation: Lectures are great for blasting through a lot of theory quickly, but they don't give you much hands-on practice or test your real-time clinical judgment. [learn more](GST321_U8_T6#GST321_U8_T6_h2)

question: What is a practical solution for QA committees when computers and digital health records are not available?

options.A: Ignoring clinical data collection entirely
options.B: Using simple, well-designed paper tracking tools and logs
options.C: Stopping all quality checks until computers are donated
options.D: Waiting for patients to remember their own medical histories

explanation: You nailed it! Good paper-based logs keep quality assurance running smoothly even when technology is missing. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h8)

question: Calculate the flow rate: 1000 mL of normal saline over 8 hours using tubing with a drop factor of 15 gtt/mL.

options.A: 60 gtt/min
options.B: 31 gtt/min
options.C: 208 gtt/min
options.D: 125 gtt/min

explanation: Math time! Multiply total volume (1000) by drop factor (15) to get 15,000. Divide by total minutes (480 mins in 8 hours), which gives 31.25—round it down to 31 drops per minute. You've got this! [learn more](GNS125_U3_T5#GNS125_U3_T5_h7)

question: Which breath sound is described as a continuous musical whistle heard when airways are narrowed?

options.A: Crackles
options.B: Wheezes
options.C: Rhonchi
options.D: Stridor

explanation: Wheezes are high-pitched musical sounds created when air flows through constricted bronchial tubes. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T10#GNS213_U2_T10_h6)

question: What is a key nursing duty during the post-disaster recovery phase?

options.A: Monitoring for delayed health issues like infectious disease outbreaks
options.B: Stopping all documentation of past emergency responses
options.C: Discontinuing all community health education programs permanently
options.D: Closing down local clinics indefinitely

explanation: You got it! Even after the dust settles, crowded conditions and dirty water pose major risks, so nurses must stay alert for disease outbreaks. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T2#GNS315_U1_T2_h8)

question: How do illnesses often show up in older adults compared to younger people?

options.A: By producing no physical changes whatsoever
options.B: With much higher fevers and severe localized pain
options.C: As subtle changes like sudden confusion or mild fatigue
options.D: Through rapid weight gain in a single day

explanation: Spot on! Older adults often show 'atypical' symptoms. Instead of a classic high fever, a simple infection might first make them unusually sleepy or confused. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T3#GNS324_U3_T3_h2)

question: A patient recovering from a severe stroke struggles to walk and needs help rebuilding muscle strength. Which team member should be consulted?

options.A: Physician
options.B: Physiotherapist
options.C: Pharmacist
options.D: Social worker

explanation: You nailed it! Physiotherapists are experts at helping patients regain movement, strength, and independence after major setbacks like strokes. [learn more](GST321_U7_T2#GST321_U7_T2_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a major barrier to stopping FGM in Nigeria?

options.A: The practice being driven underground into hidden spots
options.B: Deep-seated patriarchal norms and fear of social stigma
options.C: Not having enough funding for state anti-FGM task forces
options.D: Universal public support and open reporting from every local community

explanation: You nailed it! There is no universal public support for FGM. Rather, secrecy, fear of stigma, and poor funding are the real barriers holding back progress. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T7#GNS312_U1_T7_h7)

question: What happens to a diagnostic skin test if the nurse accidentally injects the medication into the subcutaneous layer?

options.A: The medication crystallizes under the skin and causes infection.
options.B: The patient develops immediate anaphylactic shock.
options.C: The reaction becomes much larger and easier to read.
options.D: The test becomes invalid because the drug absorbs too quickly.

explanation: Subcutaneous tissue has more blood supply, causing rapid absorption that ruins the localized delayed immune reaction needed for a valid test. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h6)

question: After a safe delivery, which eye ointment do you apply right away to protect a newborn from eye infections?

options.A: Atropine sulfate drops
options.B: Chloramphenicol eye drops
options.C: Hydrocortisone eye gel
options.D: Tetracycline eye ointment

explanation: Brilliant! Tetracycline 1% eye ointment is standard care to shield baby's eyes from harmful bacteria passed during birth. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T11#GNS225_U3_T11_h6)

question: When an adverse event happens, what is the main goal of using 'systems thinking'?

options.A: Focusing entirely on disciplining the nurse who made the final error
options.B: Reducing the number of nursing staff on duty during night shifts
options.C: Moving away from blaming individuals toward fixing workflow processes
options.D: Assuming that technology can completely eliminate all human mistakes

explanation: Systems thinking stops the blame game. Instead of pointing fingers at a colleague, it looks at the environment and structural issues that allowed the error to happen in the first place. [learn more](GST319_U5_T8#GST319_U5_T8_h3)

question: What is the safest sleeping position to teach parents to prevent SIDS (cot death)?

options.A: On the back (supine position)
options.B: On the stomach (prone position)
options.C: On either side with rolled towels
options.D: Upright in a soft infant seat

explanation: Always back to sleep! Placing babies flat on their backs for naps and bedtime is the safest way to keep their airways clear and lower the risk of SIDS. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T014#GNS226_U3_T014_h7)

question: When does everyday worry cross the line into a clinical anxiety disorder?

options.A: Normal worry only occurs in children and teenagers.
options.B: Normal worry never causes physical symptoms like a racing heart.
options.C: Clinical anxiety persists excessively and disrupts daily functioning.
options.D: Clinical anxiety disappears immediately once a stressor is removed.

explanation: We all worry about exams or finances sometimes! But clinical anxiety hangs around stubbornly and makes it hard to get through daily life. Spotting this difference helps you understand when a patient truly needs support. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T10#GNS123_U3_T10_h1)

question: Why is a damp hospital utility room a bad place to store loose tablets?

options.A: Patients will accidentally steal the medications while bathing
options.B: The bright white tiles reflect too much light onto the bottles
options.C: Hospital cleaners use harsh chemicals that change room gravity
options.D: High moisture levels promote chemical and physical breakdown of drugs

explanation: Moisture is an enemy to many dry medicines! It causes tablets to absorb water, clump together, and lose their healing power. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T4#GNS125_U4_T4_h2)

question: A patient on chemotherapy has a very low white blood cell count. What is the top nursing priority?

options.A: Stopping the process of metastasis
options.B: Giving medication to help hair grow back
options.C: Preparing the patient for emergency surgery
options.D: Monitoring closely for signs of infection

explanation: Brilliant nursing judgment! Low white blood cells (neutropenia) mean the immune system is weak, so watching for and preventing infection is your #1 priority. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T5#GNS321_U1_T5_h8)

question: What is the main advantage of using validation therapy with a patient who has dementia?

options.A: It forces the patient to remember exact dates and times
options.B: It proves to the patient that their memories are false
options.C: It cures the underlying brain disease within a few weeks
options.D: It acknowledges their feelings and helps reduce agitation

explanation: Instead of arguing with a confused patient, validation therapy respects their feelings. This keeps them calm, safe, and feeling understood. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T3#GNS324_U3_T3_h7)

question: Why does severe peripheral vascular disease often lead to an amputation?

options.A: Blocked arteries prevent oxygen and nutrients from reaching tissues, causing cell death.
options.B: High blood pressure forces the limb to swell until the skin splits open.
options.C: Excess fluid builds up in the muscles and causes the bone to snap.
options.D: Weakened veins allow blood to pool and turn into dangerous blood clots.

explanation: Think of it like a plant without water—when blood flow is cut off, the tissue lacks oxygen and dies, which can create gangrene that requires surgery. Great job learning the basics! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T12#GNS324_U4_T12_h1)

question: Why should a nurse assess a patient's swallowing ability before giving oral pills?

options.A: To prevent choking and potential aspiration into the lungs
options.B: To see if the patient has any food allergies
options.C: To check how fast the liver will metabolize the drug
options.D: To determine if the patient prefers liquid or solid medicines

explanation: Swallowing difficulties place patients at high risk of aspirating foreign objects or liquids into the respiratory tract. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T2#GNS122_U1_T2_h4)

question: Which waste product in a U&E panel comes directly from normal muscle breakdown?

options.A: Albumin
options.B: Urea
options.C: Bicarbonate
options.D: Creatinine

explanation: Well done! Creatinine is a natural byproduct of your everyday muscle activity that healthy kidneys filter right out of the blood. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T9#GNS123_U2_T9_h2)

question: Which type of teeth are primarily designed for biting and cutting food?

options.A: Incisors
options.B: Canines
options.C: Premolars
options.D: Molars

explanation: Incisors are the sharp, flat front teeth used specifically for biting off pieces of food. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T1#GNS121_U1_T1_h4)

question: Why do we use Boolean words like AND and OR when searching research databases?

options.A: To automatically translate foreign language articles into English
options.B: To convert secondary research summaries into primary data tables
options.C: To check if the author of a research paper has a valid license
options.D: To narrow or broaden search results to find relevant articles

explanation: Great work! Words like AND and OR help you filter your search so you don't get drowned in millions of unrelated papers. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T6#GNS217_U3_T6_h6)

question: A patient living near farm animals comes in with a suspected zoonotic infection. What is the best health advice to give them?

options.A: Tell them never to take medications for animal scratches
options.B: Suggest getting rid of every single animal in the neighborhood
options.C: Teach them safe food handling and how to protect themselves around animals
options.D: Tell them humans only catch things from other humans

explanation: Good hygiene, safe food prep, and protective gear go a long way in keeping animal germs away from humans. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T5#GNS313_U1_T5_h4)

question: What is the primary reason nurses 'cohort' patients in a hospital ward?

options.A: To make it easier for doctors to prescribe the exact same medication
options.B: To ensure that patients with different diseases share recovery rooms
options.C: To group patients with the same infection together to contain transmission
options.D: To reduce the total number of nursing staff required on the ward

explanation: Cohorting means putting patients with the exact same bug in one designated area so they don't spread it to uninfected patients. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T82#GNS214_U1_T82_h7)

question: An AED has just been brought to the side of an adult patient in cardiac arrest. What is the very first thing the nurse should do with it?

options.A: Press the shock button
options.B: Apply the electrode pads
options.C: Check the battery level
options.D: Turn the AED on

explanation: Turning the device on activates the audio and visual prompts that guide the rest of the rescue steps. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T1#GNS212_U2_T1_h6)

question: What pocket of pus can develop near the fallopian tube and ovary during a bad pelvic infection?

options.A: Cervical retention nodule
options.B: Endometrial polyp
options.C: Uterine fibroid cyst
options.D: Tubo-ovarian abscess

explanation: When upper reproductive infections get severe, pus can collect and form a painful pocket involving both the tube and the ovary, called a tubo-ovarian abscess. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h3)

question: You forget to give a BP medication, but the patient thankfully suffers no harm. Which element of malpractice is missing here?

options.A: Breach
options.B: Damages
options.C: Duty
options.D: Causation

explanation: Even though a mistake happened, if the patient didn't suffer any actual harm or injury, a damages claim won't hold up. [learn more](GST321_U10_T7#GST321_U10_T7_h3)

question: A Hindu patient asks for a strict vegetarian meal and refuses beef. What is the cultural background for this?

options.A: Hospital kitchens are considered impure by Hindu custom
options.B: Vegetarianism is required only during the winter months
options.C: Cows are viewed as sacred animals, and beef is strictly prohibited
options.D: All animal products are forbidden to prevent spiritual pollution

explanation: In Hinduism, cows hold a very sacred and respected status, making beef consumption a taboo for many observant followers. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T019#GNS227_U2_T019_h5)

question: How often should a bedbound patient typically be repositioned to prevent pressure ulcers?

options.A: Once every twenty-four hours
options.B: Every six hours
options.C: At least every two hours
options.D: Only when the patient asks

explanation: Turning a bedbound patient every two hours relieves continuous pressure on vulnerable skin areas and maintains blood flow. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T10#GNS225_U5_T10_h6)

question: How does a demand pacemaker operate during a normal heart rhythm?

options.A: It pumps extra blood to compensate for the fast natural rhythm
options.B: It shuts down completely and must be manually restarted by a doctor
options.C: It continuously sends rapid shocks to speed up the normal heartbeat
options.D: It remains idle and only fires when the natural heart rate drops too low

explanation: Demand pacemakers monitor the heart's natural electrical signals and only step in when the rate falls below the programmed threshold. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h2)

question: A patient has an injury damaging the nerve fibers in their ventral root. What would you expect to see?

options.A: Inability to move the target muscle effector
options.B: Inability of receptors to detect hot temperatures
options.C: Loss of sensation to pinprick in the skin
options.D: Total loss of conscious thought and memory

explanation: Since the ventral root carries the outgoing 'action' command to muscles, damaging it blocks that final signal, leading to weakness or trouble moving. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T25#GNS211_U3_T25_h5)

question: What was the main goal of classical management theory in the workplace?

options.A: Emotional counseling for all employees
options.B: Efficiency and standardized tasks
options.C: Flexible work hours and remote shifts
options.D: Democratic voting on all organizational policies

explanation: Classical management was all about maximum speed, clear chains of command, and doing tasks the exact same way every time like a machine. [learn more](GST321_U1_T1#GST321_U1_T1_h2)

question: Which of these is a classic example of a microvascular (small blood vessel) complication of diabetes?

options.A: Diabetic retinopathy affecting the eyes
options.B: Peripheral vascular disease in the legs
options.C: Coronary artery disease leading to angina
options.D: Cerebrospinal stroke affecting speech

explanation: Retinopathy damages the tiny, delicate blood vessels in the eyes, which makes it a classic microvascular complication. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T17#GNS324_U4_T17_h7)

question: What would happen if the articular cartilage at the ends of your bones wore away completely?

options.A: The joint would produce too much fluid and swell instantly
options.B: The joint would lock permanently straight
options.C: Muscles would immediately lose their ability to contract
options.D: Bone surfaces would grind directly against each other, causing pain

explanation: Spot on! Cartilage is a smooth shock absorber. Without it, bare bones rub together, causing the pain and stiffness we see in arthritis. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T7#GNS121_U3_T7_h5)

question: A working mother needs daytime care for her two-year-old toddler. Which facility type is most appropriate?

options.A: An adult day care centre
options.B: A university lecture hall
options.C: A residential boarding home
options.D: An infant and toddler nursery

explanation: A two-year-old falls into the toddler category, making an infant and toddler nursery the correct setting for age-appropriate physical care and safety. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h3)

question: Why should a nurse researcher investigate an outlier rather than deleting it immediately?

options.A: Outliers always improve the accuracy of statistical tests
options.B: It proves that the measurement scale was ordinal
options.C: Deleting data is illegal in all health research
options.D: It might represent a genuine, important clinical finding

explanation: An extreme value might look like an error at first glance, but it could actually reflect a real, critical clinical event that deserves attention. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T2#GNS224_U2_T2_h7)

question: What is the primary role of traditional and religious leaders in policy implementation?

options.A: Aiding social mobilization and gaining community acceptance
options.B: Drafting legal amendments for the national parliament
options.C: Conducting surgical family planning procedures in clinics
options.D: Auditing government budgets for health infrastructure

explanation: People trust their local and religious leaders. When these leaders support health initiatives, community members are much more open to listening and participating. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T007#GNS226_U6_T007_h6)

question: What causes pressure to build up inside a muscle compartment during compartment syndrome?

options.A: Pressure rises because the surrounding fascia cannot stretch.
options.B: Muscles dissolve completely into liquid inside the limb.
options.C: Excess air gets trapped beneath the subcutaneous fat.
options.D: The bone grows too fast and cracks the outer skin layer.

explanation: Fascia acts like a tough, unyielding wrapper around our muscles. When swelling or bleeding happens inside, that wrapper cannot expand, so pressure shoots up rapidly! [learn more](GNS222_U1_T23#GNS222_U1_T23_h4)

question: Which lifestyle habit is crucial to screen for because it directly harms a developing baby during pregnancy?

options.A: Drinking filtered tap water
options.B: Eating green leafy vegetables
options.C: Using tobacco products
options.D: Walking thirty minutes daily

explanation: Tobacco smoke carries harmful toxins that cut down blood flow to the womb and pose serious risks to an unborn baby. Always a key lifestyle question! [learn more](GNS311_U1_T3#GNS311_U1_T3_h7)

question: Most primary brain tumors start growing from which type of supportive cells in the nervous system?

options.A: Neurons
options.B: Glial cells
options.C: Bone cells
options.D: Blood vessels

explanation: Spot on! While neurons get all the fame for sending nerve signals, most primary brain tumors actually arise from glial cells—the supportive glue and caretaker cells of the brain. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T14#GNS222_U3_T14_h2)

question: Which substance must be present in the stomach for vitamin B12 to be absorbed properly?

options.A: Hydrochloric acid
options.B: Bile salt binding
options.C: Intrinsic factor
options.D: Pepsinogen enzyme

explanation: Intrinsic factor is a special helper made by the stomach that binds to vitamin B12 so it can safely travel and be absorbed down the line. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T6#GNS223_U1_T6_h3)

question: Why is it important to involve community members at every step of an advocacy project?

options.A: It prevents government officials from visiting the health center
options.B: It relieves the nurse from doing any paperwork or reporting
options.C: It ensures that the nurse receives financial compensation from villagers
options.D: It builds local ownership so the community sustains the change long-term

explanation: Spot on! When people help fix their own problems, they take pride in the results and keep the good work going long after the nurse leaves. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T14#GNS225_U2_T14_h7)

question: Where is the nurses' station typically placed in a modern hospital ward?

options.A: At the center to allow clear sightlines
options.B: Near the entrance to restrict visitor access
options.C: At the far end away from patient beds
options.D: Inside the main doctor consulting room

explanation: Central placement helps staff monitor patient activity and respond quickly to call bells or emergencies. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h2)

question: Why should a nurse quickly check the patient in person when the monitor shows a sudden weird rhythm?

options.A: To determine if the patient needs an immediate dose of insulin
options.B: To calculate the exact cardiac output of the ventricles
options.C: To check if the intravenous line has become infiltrated
options.D: To rule out artifact caused by movement or loose cables

explanation: Always treat the patient, not just the monitor screen! Shivering, moving around, or a loose cable can make the screen look terrifying even when the patient is totally fine. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T17#GNS213_U1_T17_h7)

question: When giving a bed bath, which direction should you always wash the patient's body?

options.A: From the legs up straight to the face
options.B: From the sides toward the back spine
options.C: From the most sensitive parts to the least sensitive
options.D: From the cleanest areas to the dirtiest areas

explanation: Brilliant! Always start with the cleanest parts (like the face) and move down so you don't drag dirt and germs onto clean skin. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h2)

question: What is the best way for doctors to find out exactly which germ is causing a newborn's eye infection?

options.A: Complete blood count with differential
options.B: Conjunctival swabs for culture and staining
options.C: Ultrasound imaging of the eyeball
options.D: Routine measurement of intraocular pressure

explanation: Correct! Taking a gentle swab of the eye discharge lets the lab tell us the exact culprit so the right treatment can be given. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T019#GNS226_U3_T019_h4)

question: How do hard scars (plaques) cause symptoms in disseminated sclerosis?

options.A: They cause excess production of spinal fluid in the brain ventricles
options.B: They stimulate muscles to contract constantly without rest
options.C: They repair the damaged nerves completely back to normal
options.D: They block and slow down electrical signals traveling along nerve fibers

explanation: When inflammation creates scar tissue (plaques), it gets in the way of smooth electrical conduction—leading to the physical and sensory changes patients feel. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T3#GNS222_U4_T3_h2)

question: How would you simply describe an autoimmune disease?

options.A: A condition where the immune system attacks the body's own healthy tissues
options.B: A temporary infection spread through close contact in a community
options.C: An immediate allergic reaction caused by exposure to environmental pollen
options.D: A genetic deficiency that prevents the production of red blood cells

explanation: In autoimmune diseases, the immune system gets confused and mistakenly treats friendly, healthy body cells as enemies, attacking them by mistake. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T14#GNS111_U2_T14_h7)

question: What is the main problem in the body when someone has anaemia?

options.A: Increased thickness of the blood plasma
options.B: Rapid destruction of blood platelets
options.C: Too many white blood cells
options.D: Reduced oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood

explanation: You've got this! Anaemia simply means the blood doesn't have enough red blood cells or hemoglobin to carry the oxygen your body needs to function well. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T6#GNS311_U2_T6_h1)

question: Why is a tension pneumothorax such a major emergency?

options.A: Trapped air builds up pressure and shifts the heart and major blood vessels

options.C: It floods both lungs with thick, yellow mucus
options.D: It causes an immediate massive infection in the bronchial tubes

explanation: Correct! Trapped air keeps stacking up like a balloon, pushing everything in the chest sideways and stopping blood from returning to the heart. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T12#GNS213_U2_T12_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of giving a patient a purgative?

options.A: To increase the absorption of water in the large intestine
options.B: To slow down gastrointestinal motility and prevent diarrhea
options.C: To promote bowel movements and relieve constipation
options.D: To neutralize excess stomach acid and soothe ulcers

explanation: You've got this! Purgatives are simply given to help clear the bowels and get things moving when a patient is constipated. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T2#GNS223_U3_T2_h1)

question: Which major part of the adult brain develops directly from the telencephalon?

options.A: Cerebrum
options.B: Pons
options.C: Thalamus
options.D: Medulla oblongata

explanation: The telencephalon is the part of the early brain that grows and expands to form our large cerebrum and its two halves. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T7#GNS211_U3_T7_h1)

question: Which nursing theory focuses heavily on helping a person or community practice self-care?

options.A: Florence Nightingale's Environmental Theory
options.B: Dorothea Orem's Self-Care Deficit Theory
options.C: Sigmund Freud's Psychosexual Theory
options.D: Abraham Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs

explanation: Spot on! Orem's model is all about empowering people with the skills they need to take charge of their own health. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T7#GNS225_U2_T7_h6)

question: In which section of the fallopian tube does fertilization usually occur?

options.A: Ampulla
options.B: Fimbriae
options.C: Isthmus
options.D: Cervix

explanation: The ampulla is the wide middle section where sperm and egg typically meet and fertilize. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T2#GNS121_U5_T2_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard duty for a clinical nurse regarding waste management?

options.A: Educating patients on safe disposal of personal medical items
options.B: Designing and building new municipal waste landfills
options.C: Reporting damaged or overfilled sharp containers
options.D: Segregating items into appropriate colored bins

explanation: Correct! Building landfills is the job of civil and environmental engineers, not clinical nurses. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h7)

question: What is a key role of a community health nurse when working alongside NGOs?

options.A: Manufacturing medical vaccines in hospital laboratories
options.B: Acting as a bridge between visiting volunteers and local patients
options.C: Auditing the international bank accounts of donor agencies

question: Why are community health nurses considered the frontline eyes and ears of health surveillance?

options.A: They have direct, daily contact with patients and local communities
options.B: They manage the federal budget for disease control programs
options.C: They spend most of their working hours analyzing computer software

question: What is the role of the falx cerebri inside the skull?

options.C: It forms a tight seal to prevent any blood from entering the brain.

question: What is evaluated during a functional assessment prior to admission?

options.A: Financial credit history
options.B: Workplace performance record
options.C: Previous travel experiences
options.D: Activities of daily living

explanation: A functional assessment looks closely at how well a potential resident can manage basic daily self-care tasks like bathing and dressing. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h2)

question: When counseling pregnant women about traditional food habits, which approach is NOT helpful?

options.A: Listening carefully to the patient's family and cultural beliefs
options.B: Incorporating affordable local staples like beans and dark leafy greens
options.C: Identifying harmful taboos without disrespecting the community
options.D: Insisting that only imported foreign foods can provide proper prenatal nutrition

explanation: Spot on! Good nursing care relies on affordable, local foods that everyday families can actually get, not expensive foreign items. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T008#GNS227_U2_T008_h7)

question: When do vulval varicose veins most commonly show up?

options.A: During puberty
options.B: Immediately after menstruation
options.C: After menopause
options.D: During pregnancy

explanation: Pregnancy is the peak time for this! The body increases its blood volume and puts extra pressure in the pelvis, which makes these veins pop up. Great job thinking through prenatal changes. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T9#GNS216_U5_T9_h1)

question: Which of these is an actual 'system-level' fix to improve patient safety?

options.A: Redesigning electronic medication screens to make high-risk doses harder to select

options.C: Posting a memo on the staff bulletin board about being careful
options.D: Suspending the nurse involved in the error for a period of two weeks

explanation: That's a true system fix! Changing how a computer system or tool works makes doing the right thing much easier and mistakes much harder to make. [learn more](GST319_U5_T2#GST319_U5_T2_h6)

question: How does an additive drug interaction work?

options.A: The combined effect equals the sum of individual effects
options.B: The drugs completely destroy each other in the bloodstream
options.C: The combined effect is lower than either single drug
options.D: The combined effect is much greater than individual effects

explanation: An additive effect is straightforward: 1 + 1 = 2! The drugs simply add their normal effects together without extra superpowers. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T6#GNS125_U5_T6_h2)

question: Two clinical instructors use the exact same rubric to grade your wound dressing, but their scores are wildly different. What does this point to?

options.A: Construct validity
options.B: Content bias
options.C: Formative timing
options.D: Inter-rater reliability

explanation: When different teachers get different scores using the exact same tool on the same student, the tool has an issue with inter-rater reliability. You are mastering the nursing jargon! [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h8)

question: Which gender-related pressure often leads to higher rates of sexually transmitted infections among young males?

options.A: Strict adherence to solitary domestic lifestyles
options.B: Complete abstinence from all social gatherings
options.C: Fear of asking healthcare workers for vitamins
options.D: Pressure to prove masculinity through multiple partners

explanation: That's right! Societal pressure telling boys they must have multiple partners to 'prove' their manhood can unfortunately spread infections quickly. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T11#GNS312_U3_T11_h5)

question: Why do nurses check routine blood tests for medical-surgical patients?

options.A: To replace the need for physical head-to-toe assessments
options.B: To permanently cure chronic underlying disease processes
options.C: To measure the exact total volume of blood in the body
options.D: To monitor physiological shifts and evaluate organ function

explanation: Blood tests are like a window into the body! They give you clear clues on how well internal organs are coping, helping you track your patient's recovery day by day. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T7#GNS123_U2_T7_h1)

question: What is the main job of our skin, hair, and nails (the integumentary system)?

options.A: Regulating red blood cell production in bone marrow
options.B: Facilitating conscious voluntary muscle movement
options.C: Synthesizing essential water-soluble vitamins
options.D: Protecting the body from environmental hazards

explanation: Think of your skin as your body's personal security guard! It is your first line of defense against germs, harsh chemicals, and physical injury. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T2#GNS213_U5_T2_h1)

question: As a nurse leader, why is it important to understand the psychology behind workplace changes?

options.A: To completely eliminate all feelings of stress in the hospital
options.B: To ensure that no clinical protocols are ever modified again
options.C: To view resistance as a normal reaction instead of laziness
options.D: To punish staff members who fail to adopt new policies

explanation: Spot on! When leaders understand this, they can approach staff hesitation with empathy and support rather than frustration. [learn more](GST319_U2_T5#GST319_U2_T5_h1)

question: At what age does a baby get their first dose of the measles vaccine?

options.A: At 9 months of age
options.B: At birth
options.C: At 6 weeks of age
options.D: At 14 weeks of age

explanation: Exactly! We wait until 9 months because antibodies passed down from the mother can block the measles vaccine if given too early. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T63#GNS214_U1_T63_h2)

question: Which of these is a duty of nursing management rather than leadership?

options.A: Challenging outdated hospital traditions to improve care
options.B: Mentoring junior staff to find their professional purpose
options.C: Inspiring colleagues to embrace a new clinical vision
options.D: Creating staff shift schedules and managing budgets

explanation: Spot on! Management focuses on the day-to-day operations like rotas and resources, while leadership focuses on inspiration and big-picture vision. [learn more](GST321_U3_T1#GST321_U3_T1_h2)

question: What sign of infection should a patient on chemo report right away?

options.A: A low-grade fever or chills
options.B: Dry skin on the hands
options.C: Mild fatigue after walking
options.D: Slight thinning of head hair

explanation: Spot on! Even a small fever is an emergency for a chemo patient because their immune system is too weak to fight germs easily. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T7#GNS215_U6_T7_h8)

question: What is the main job of the vagina in the female body?

options.A: Producing female sex hormones
options.B: Storing eggs before fertilization
options.C: Filtering waste products from blood
options.D: Connecting the vulva to the cervix

explanation: You got this! The vagina is simply a muscular canal that acts as a direct passageway between the outside (vulva) and the uterus (via the cervix). [learn more](GNS216_U5_T11#GNS216_U5_T11_h1)

question: A male patient is diagnosed with an indirect inguinal hernia. Which nearby anatomical structure is most at risk of compression within the inguinal canal?

options.A: Spermatic cord contents
options.B: Corporis cavernosa
options.C: Urinary bladder neck
options.D: Bulbourethral glands

explanation: Because the spermatic cord passes directly through the inguinal canal, a hernia in this area can compress the vessels and nerves within the cord. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T2#GNS216_U2_T2_h4)

question: What is the most common cause of a high-pressure ventilator alarm?

options.A: A sudden massive air leak in the circuit
options.B: The patient has stopped breathing completely
options.C: Obstruction, coughing, or tube kinking
options.D: Disconnection of the ventilator tubing

explanation: A high-pressure alarm means the machine is struggling to push air in because something is blocking the path—like thick mucus, the patient biting the tube, or a kink in the tubing. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T6#GNS315_U3_T6_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT an expected result of taking a sympathomimetic drug?

options.A: Pupil dilation
options.B: Bronchodilation
options.C: Increased heart rate
options.D: Decreased heart rate

explanation: Sympathomimetic drugs mimic the sympathetic system—they speed things up, open airways, and widen pupils. They won't slow down the heart rate! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T30#GNS211_U3_T30_h6)

question: What is the main goal of diet therapy in patient care?

options.A: Modifying regular food intake to meet specific health needs
options.B: Reducing hospital kitchen operational costs
options.C: Ensuring every patient eats the exact same meal
options.D: Replacing all forms of medical drug treatment

explanation: You've got this! Diet therapy is simply tailoring a patient's nutrition to help them heal, manage an illness, or balance their body's needs. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T22#GNS214_U1_T22_h1)

question: Which type of gauze is specially designed to fit snugly around a surgical drain?

options.A: Split-drain gauze with a pre-cut slit
options.B: Elastic compression bandage wraps
options.C: Large roller gauze wrapped around the limb

question: Why would a bleeding disorder make a liver biopsy unsafe?

question: What is the main focus of efficiency in a healthcare plan?

options.A: Getting maximum results with minimum waste of resources
options.B: Spending the entire annual budget before the year ends
options.C: Employing as many administrative workers as possible
options.D: Purchasing the most expensive medical equipment available

explanation: Efficiency is all about making the best use of limited supplies, money, and staff time without unnecessary waste. [learn more](GST321_U1_T7#GST321_U1_T7_h6)

question: Which group is usually formed by local neighbors to tackle specific health needs in their area?

options.A: Community-Based Organizations
options.B: International pharmaceutical firms

options.D: Federal ministries of health

question: What is the main difference between cleaning a kitchen surface and sanitizing it?

options.A: Cleaning removes visible dirt and grease while sanitizing reduces microorganisms to safe levels.

options.C: Cleaning is done after food preparation while sanitizing must be done before cooking.

question: What is the main job of the muscle layer in the ureter wall?

question: How do RFID tags help clinical staff manage equipment?

question: Why do we encourage skin-to-skin contact right after a normal delivery?

question: What does reproductive health cover according to standard health definitions?

question: What is the main goal of having a menu in a hospital or clinic kitchen?

question: Why are hospitals so keen to collect and study near-miss reports?

question: Why do we check two patient identifiers before giving any medication?

question: Which symptom is a classic warning sign of potential postpartum preeclampsia at home?

question: Why would a cell decide to do receptor downregulation?

question: Why is teaching such a huge part of a home health nurse's job?

question: A patient catches a hookworm infection after walking barefoot on damp, contaminated soil. How did the parasite get in?

question: Which official body holds Nigerian nurses legally accountable for their practice?

question: Which level of disinfection is needed to reliably kill Mycobacterium tuberculosis on a semi-critical tool?

question: What is the main goal of doing a 'review of systems' during an assessment?

question: How do community support groups help individuals living with diabetes?

options.B: By reducing isolation and sharing practical coping strategies

question: What is a major advantage of Rapid Diagnostic Tests in primary health care?

question: A nurse uses a single-dose medication vial for three different patients to save time. How would you classify this action?

options.C: A standard emergency protocol

question: A nurse thinks safety rules only matter in big factories and ignores small offices in the building. Where is the mistake in this thinking?

question: Which muscle action is responsible for moving waste along the colon?

question: A patient with sickle cell anaemia is admitted in a painful vaso-occlusive crisis. Which immediate nursing intervention should be prioritized?

question: What is a super important piece of discharge teaching for a patient on antibiotics for a bone infection?

question: Why do we test changes on a small scale using the PDSA cycle first?

question: What is a great natural food source of folic acid?

options.D: Processed red meat

question: What is the main purpose of a Root Cause Analysis (RCA)?

options.C: To investigate why an error occurred by identifying underlying system flaws
options.D: To evaluate the daily bedside performance of individual students

explanation: RCA is like detective work! It looks deep into the system to find out why a mistake happened, rather than just pointing fingers at a person. [learn more](GST319_U5_T5#GST319_U5_T5_h7)

question: In very poor communities, what is one of the most common reasons families push young daughters into early marriage?

question: A client using a combined oral contraceptive pill develops severe throbbing headaches and high blood pressure. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

question: What serious long-term problem can happen if severe, chronic anaemia is ignored?

question: Why do nurse researchers rely so much on a theoretical framework?

options.D: It eliminates the need for statistical data analysis entirely

question: Why do nurses advise wearing cotton underwear when dealing with a yeast infection?

options.C: Cotton fibers directly release natural antifungal chemicals onto the skin
options.D: Synthetic fabrics chemically bind to antifungal creams and block their action

question: Why is home delivery not recommended as a default option for every pregnant woman?

options.B: Hospitals prefer to keep all pregnant women admitted
options.C: Unforeseen complications can arise suddenly during labor

question: Why does damage to the central nervous system usually affect the whole body more drastically than an injury to a single peripheral nerve?

options.C: The CNS does not have protective meninges.

question: How often should you check the patient's breathing during the early phase of steam therapy?

question: What do we call the exact spot on an antigen that an antibody latches onto?

question: Why does long-term low blood oxygen sometimes lead to secondary polycythemia?

question: A patient with a leg cast complains of a sharp, burning pain in one spot underneath. What stockinette issue could be causing this?

question: What do we call weakness affecting one entire side of the body, often seen after a stroke?

options.D: Paraplegia

question: Which hormone signals the Leydig cells in the testes to make testosterone?

options.C: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH)
options.D: Prostate-specific antigen (PSA)

explanation: You've got this! Luteinizing hormone (LH) travels from the brain's pituitary gland down to the testes, giving the green light for testosterone production. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T1#GNS311_U1_T1_h5)

question: How should removable dentures be kept when the patient is not wearing them?

options.B: In a labeled container filled with water or soaking solution
options.C: Dropped in boiling water overnight to kill all germs
options.D: Left out in the open air on top of the locker table

explanation: Keeping dentures wet in a safe container stops the plastic material from bending out of shape and keeps them ready for use. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T3#GNS112_U5_T3_h6)

question: A patient needs a very early pregnancy test using urine. Which sample should you tell her to collect?

options.A: First morning urine
options.B: Timed two-hour urine
options.C: Random afternoon urine
options.D: Post-exercise urine

explanation: First morning urine is the most concentrated, meaning any early pregnancy hormones will be nice and strong and easy for the test to pick up! [learn more](GNS123_U2_T6#GNS123_U2_T6_h2)

question: What is the main job of the anterior pituitary gland in the neuroendocrine system?

options.A: It generates electrical impulses for sympathetic flight responses
options.B: It monitors blood glucose levels via direct humoral sensation
options.C: It releases tropic hormones in response to hypothalamic signals
options.D: It stores oxytocin and antidiuretic hormone produced by neurons

explanation: The anterior pituitary takes messages from the hypothalamus and releases its own hormones to control other glands in the body. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T6#GNS211_U1_T6_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of the Annual Performance Evaluation Report (APER) in the civil service?

options.A: To formally assess an employee's work performance, conduct, and suitability for promotion
options.B: To track the disbursement of pharmaceutical supplies across hospital wards
options.C: To calculate the monthly personal income tax deductions for healthcare workers
options.D: To record the daily patient census managed by a specific nursing unit

explanation: The APER form is filled out yearly by your boss to check your work ethic, attitude, and readiness to move up the career ladder. [learn more](GST321_U10_T1#GST321_U10_T1_h6)

question: Why does limiting the number of available medicines improve a health system?

options.A: It completely eliminates the risk of patient allergic reactions
options.B: It forces doctors to prescribe only expensive imported brands
options.C: It guarantees that pharmaceutical companies stop manufacturing
options.D: It lowers costs and makes medicine supply easier to manage

explanation: Carrying fewer, well-tested drugs simplifies purchasing, storage, and distribution while keeping prices affordable. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h1)

question: What do we call the solid, mulberry-like cluster of cells formed during early embryonic travel?

options.A: Pronucleus
options.B: Zygote
options.C: Morula
options.D: Blastocyst

explanation: Spot on! The morula is a solid little cluster of cells that looks a bit like a tiny mulberry as it travels down the tube. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T8#GNS121_U5_T8_h7)

question: Which of these common pain meds is a selective COX-2 inhibitor, designed to be gentler on the stomach?

options.A: Naproxen
options.B: Diclofenac
options.C: Ibuprofen
options.D: Celecoxib

explanation: Celecoxib is specially engineered to target only the COX-2 enzyme (which causes pain and inflammation) while leaving the stomach-protecting COX-1 alone. Clever drug design! [learn more](GNS223_U5_T4#GNS223_U5_T4_h2)

question: A study shows that talking patients through what to expect before surgery reduces their anxiety. What is the best next step?

options.A: Hide the research report so patients do not ask questions about surgery
options.B: Update hospital ward routines to include structured education before surgery
options.C: Stop giving pain medication to surgical patients entirely
options.D: Ignore the study results because they are based on words instead of numbers

explanation: When research proves a simple practice helps patients feel better, the best move is to put it into action on the ward! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T16#GNS217_U3_T16_h6)

question: Which action best demonstrates the nurse's role in interprofessional drug information exchange?

options.A: Consulting with the hospital pharmacist to clarify an ambiguous drug dosage order
options.B: Writing the discharge prescription without consulting the medical team
options.C: Changing a patient's medication dose independently when side effects appear
options.D: Deciding which new drugs the hospital pharmacy committee should purchase

explanation: Working closely with pharmacists ensures safe medication practices through collaborative communication. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T3#GNS215_U2_T3_h5)

question: Which health worker is best at helping a patient relearn daily tasks like bathing, dressing, and cooking?

options.A: Occupational therapist
options.B: Pharmacist
options.C: Physiotherapist
options.D: Speech pathologist

explanation: Great job! Occupational therapists focus heavily on everyday living activities and finding smart ways to adapt tasks so the patient can manage on their own. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T17#GNS225_U5_T17_h3)

question: Why is nurse coordination so important when a patient is seeing multiple medical specialists?

options.A: To perform advanced surgical procedures in community clinics
options.B: To reduce the financial cost of private specialist consultations
options.C: To replace the need for regular primary healthcare visits
options.D: To prevent conflicting treatment plans and ensure smooth communication

explanation: When too many doctors are involved, advice can clash! As nurses, we bring everything together to keep our patients safe. Brilliant teamwork! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T15#GNS225_U5_T15_h3)

question: What is cervicitis?

options.A: Infection of the uterine lining
options.B: Inflammation of the cervix
options.C: Overgrowth of normal vaginal flora
options.D: Scarring of the fallopian tubes

explanation: Cervicitis refers specifically to the inflammation of the mucosal and epithelial tissues of the cervix. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T14#GNS216_U5_T14_h1)

question: Why is keeping things confidential so vital when teaching youth about sexual health?

options.A: It prevents parents from ever speaking with healthcare providers
options.B: It is required by law only for adult patients over the age of twenty-one
options.C: It builds trust and encourages adolescents to seek necessary health guidance
options.D: It guarantees that the adolescent will never experience an illness

explanation: You got it! Teens are much more likely to ask for help and get correct information when they know their private worries are safe with you. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T19#GNS312_U3_T19_h8)

question: Which of these is NOT a benefit of strong teamwork among healthcare professionals in the community?

options.A: Better sharing of critical clinical updates
options.B: Improved support for complex family needs
options.C: Clearer understanding of each professional's role
options.D: Increased patient confusion regarding treatment plans

explanation: Good teamwork clears up confusion, it doesn't cause it! You spotted the trick question easily. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T23#GNS225_U2_T23_h7)

question: A stroke survivor struggles to button their shirt and prepare meals independently. Which therapist is best suited to address these challenges?

options.A: Medical social worker
options.B: Home health aide
options.C: Physical therapist
options.D: Occupational therapist

explanation: Occupational therapists help patients regain fine motor skills needed for activities of daily living like dressing and cooking. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why is it important to involve traditional and religious leaders in health mobilisation?

options.A: They hold strong moral authority and influence public opinion
options.B: They write the national nursing curriculum
options.C: They are the only people who understand modern medicine
options.D: They are required by law to fund all local pharmacies

explanation: Traditional and religious leaders are respected, and their approval helps community members trust health initiatives. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T1#GNS124_U4_T1_h4)

question: What is the correct chronological order of the three stages in the General Adaptation Syndrome?

options.A: Alarm, exhaustion, resistance
options.B: Resistance, alarm, exhaustion
options.C: Exhaustion, resistance, alarm
options.D: Alarm, resistance, exhaustion

explanation: The body first experiences a sudden alarm, tries to resist the ongoing stress, and finally reaches exhaustion if the stress is too prolonged. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T6#GNS123_U1_T6_h2)

question: When checking vital signs, why is it better to look at trends over time rather than a single reading?

options.A: Single readings are always completely wrong
options.B: Trends automatically calculate medication doses
options.C: A single reading can miss subtle shifts in a patient's overall condition
options.D: Isolated numbers are illegal to chart

explanation: You got it! Looking at how vitals change over time gives you a much better picture of your patient's stability than just one snapshot. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T4#GNS123_U2_T4_h1)

question: What does Gross National Product (GNP) measure?

options.A: The total amount of physical cash printed by the central bank
options.B: Only the money earned by foreign companies inside the country
options.C: The total cost of running public hospitals for one year
options.D: The total economic value produced by a country's citizens globally

explanation: Think of GNP as tracking the wealth created by a country's people, no matter where in the world they are working! You've got this. [learn more](GST322_U3_T2#GST322_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why was the team nursing model originally introduced in healthcare settings?

options.A: To completely eliminate the need for registered nurses
options.B: To cope with nursing shortages and use various staff skills efficiently
options.C: To make patients pay less money for hospital admission
options.D: To reduce the number of doctors needed in the hospital

explanation: Exactly! Team nursing was designed to make the best use of available hands when professional nurses are limited in number. It's all about smart teamwork! [learn more](GNS123_U1_T4#GNS123_U1_T4_h1)

question: How many pairs of cranial nerves emerge directly from the brain?

options.A: 31 pairs
options.B: 24 pairs

question: A patient with chronic kidney disease shows signs of metabolic acidosis. What lab result would a nurse expect to see?

options.B: An increased respiratory rate causing carbon dioxide retention
options.C: A high concentration of bicarbonate in the fresh urine
options.D: A low serum bicarbonate level on the lab report

question: Which important plasma protein helps hold water inside our blood vessels to prevent swelling?

options.A: Hemoglobin
options.B: Albumin
options.C: Fibrinogen
options.D: Alpha globulin

explanation: You got it! Albumin acts like a sponge inside your blood vessels, pulling on water to keep fluid from leaking out into the body tissues. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T1#GNS111_U2_T1_h3)

question: Why do many patients stop taking their blood pressure medication without telling their nurse?

options.A: They feel fine and assume the condition has gone away.
options.B: The medications always cure hypertension within one week.
options.C: Blood pressure pills taste sweet like candy.
options.D: Doctors prefer patients to stop taking pills after a month.

explanation: Because high blood pressure is asymptomatic, patients often mistake feeling well for being cured and abandon their regimen. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T16#GNS324_U4_T16_h5)

question: Which complication frequently develops following prolonged low blood pressure and shock from severe bleeding?

options.A: Acute kidney injury
options.B: Enlargement of the spleen
options.C: Excessive bone mineralization
options.D: Chronic high blood pressure

question: What makes the Vagus nerve (Cranial Nerve X) stand out from most other cranial nerves?

options.A: It controls the sense of smell entirely on its own.
options.B: It has no sensory function whatsoever.
options.C: It travels all the way down into the chest and tummy.
options.D: It only activates during high stress or panic.

explanation: Fantastic! While most cranial nerves stay around the head, the vagus nerve wanders down to supply our chest and belly organs. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T15#GNS211_U3_T15_h4)

question: What does 'anticipatory grief' mean?

options.A: Grief that happens before an expected loss actually occurs
options.B: Grief that completely resolves within twenty-four hours
options.C: Mourning that only affects family members rather than patients
options.D: A sudden emotional breakdown with no clear identifiable trigger

explanation: You've got this! Anticipatory grief simply means processing a loss before it happens, like when someone is facing a long terminal illness. It's totally natural. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T5#GNS221_U4_T5_h1)

question: What is the main job of sensory nerves in our body?

options.A: Producing hormones to regulate metabolic rate
options.B: Transmitting information from body tissues to the central nervous system
options.C: Carrying signals away from the brain to muscles
options.D: Controlling involuntary heart contractions

explanation: Spot on! Sensory nerves act like telephone wires, carrying messages from your skin and organs back to the brain and spinal cord so you know what's happening around you. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T28#GNS211_U3_T28_h1)

question: Think of a research design as a step-by-step plan. What is its main job in nursing?

options.A: To secure ethical approval from the hospital board
options.B: To calculate the exact financial cost of a hospital study
options.C: To write the final reference list for a journal article
options.D: To act as a blueprint for answering a clinical question

explanation: Spot on! Just like building a house needs a good plan, a research design is your overall framework that guides how you answer a specific clinical question. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T3#GNS224_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why do patients often forget to mention herbal supplements when you ask about their medications?

options.C: Federal laws prohibit patients from discussing herbs in hospitals
options.D: They do not consider supplements to be real medicine

question: Which part of the brainstem contains the main control hubs for heart rate and breathing rhythms?

options.C: Midbrain

question: Which of the following is NOT a major benefit of HMOs for patients?

options.D: Protection against sudden catastrophic out-of-pocket bills

question: What is the main goal of targeted temperature management after a patient is successfully revived?

options.C: To lower the heart rate back down to normal resting levels

question: What is considered the gold standard proof that your autoclave actually killed all microbial spores?

options.C: Chemical indicator tape placed on the outside of peel packs
options.D: Biological indicators containing resistant bacterial spores

question: What is a major reason doctors prescribe corticosteroids for lung conditions?

options.C: To kill bacterial germs inside the lungs
options.D: To lower high blood pressure in lung vessels

question: What is the expected effect of acute blood loss on a patient's pulse rate?

options.D: The pulse rhythm becomes permanently irregular and slow

question: A patient is admitted with poorly controlled high blood pressure and fluid retention. The nurse provides counselling on a low-sodium diet. What type of counselling is this?

options.B: Therapeutic and clinical counselling

question: What is the main purpose of a head-to-toe secondary survey?

options.D: To discover non-immediate or hidden injuries that the primary survey missed

explanation: Once the patient is safe from dying right away, the secondary survey helps you catch those less obvious bumps, bruises, and fractures. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T2#GNS315_U3_T2_h4)

question: What is one limitation of the placenta's protective barrier role against harmful substances?

options.C: It destroys all maternal antibodies before they reach the fetus
options.D: It completely blocks all medications taken by the mother

question: What is the best step-by-step order for a nurse trying to wake a sleeping patient during a neuro check?

options.C: Painful stimulus first, followed by loud yelling
options.D: Voice, then touch, and finally painful stimulus if needed

question: What is a 'windshield survey' in community health nursing?

options.A: Measuring air pollution levels near busy highways

options.C: Testing the windshields of ambulances for proper safety glass
options.D: Observing community conditions firsthand while moving through the area

question: How does neurasthenia mainly differ from major depression?

options.B: Depression never causes any physical tiredness or sleep changes
options.C: Depression is treated exclusively with physical exercise
options.D: Neurasthenia only occurs in children and teenagers

question: What is the medical term for an abnormally enlarged spleen?

options.A: Hepatomegaly
options.B: Lymphadenopathy
options.C: Cardiomegaly
options.D: Splenomegaly

question: How can stagnant water or soil act as a source of community infection?

options.B: By turning into clinical cases of human disease
options.C: By harboring environmental bacteria and fungal spores that enter the body
options.D: By mutating human cells to create new viruses

question: A village has had 500 total cases of diabetes for ten years, but only 5 people were newly diagnosed this year. What does this mean?

options.B: Both low prevalence and low incidence
options.C: High prevalence and low incidence

question: A patient experiences a sudden seizure that immediately affects both sides of the brain with a total loss of consciousness. How is this classified?

question: A public hospital runs out of basic drugs and asks patients to buy supplies outside. What is the main reason behind this?

options.B: Mandatory surplus funds generated by local governments
options.C: Excessive funding from international development partners
options.D: Complete elimination of out-of-pocket payments nationwide

question: Which intervention involves threading a catheter through blood vessels to block the bleeding site with tiny coils?

options.A: Interventional radiology embolization
options.B: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy
options.C: Endoscopic vessel clipping
options.D: Routine surgical wound suturing

question: What is the main goal of putting people in quarantine during an outbreak?

options.A: To cure chronic non-communicable diseases in regional health centers
options.B: To restrict movement of healthy people exposed to infection during the incubation period
options.C: To punish people who refuse to take their prescribed preventive medications
options.D: To provide specialized intensive care for patients with severe organ failure

explanation: Quarantine keeps exposed but healthy people away from others just to watch and see if symptoms show up. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T10#GNS313_U1_T10_h6)

question: What is the main public health approach used to control schistosomiasis in heavily affected communities?

options.A: Widespread daily chlorine spraying of all farmlands
options.B: Mandatory quarantine of all infected families
options.C: Mass drug administration of praziquantel
options.D: Surgical removal of adult worms from patients

explanation: Instead of waiting for individuals to fall sick, health teams treat whole communities—especially school children—all at once to knock down the disease burden. Brilliant public health strategy! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T10#GNS214_U1_T10_h8)

question: How do we describe disease spread caused by a mosquito bite?

options.A: Vector-borne transmission
options.B: Direct transmission
options.C: Airborne transmission
options.D: Vehicle-borne transmission

question: Which part of the human eye does the most work when focusing light?

options.B: The iris
options.C: The cornea
options.D: The lens

question: Why do clinical departments use standardized grading rubrics (marking guides) for procedures?

options.A: To make clinical exams optional
options.B: To cancel written care plans
options.C: To let students grade themselves
options.D: To reduce tutor bias and ensure fair grading

question: What is the main reason pregnant women are encouraged to attend routine antenatal care (ANC) visits?

options.A: To provide the mother with high doses of broad-spectrum antibiotics

options.C: To schedule the exact date and time when labor will officially begin
options.D: To monitor fetal growth and screen for conditions like anemia and high blood pressure

question: Why is follow-up after a referral so important for a community health nurse?

options.C: To audit the financial records of the tertiary hospital
options.D: To reverse the contraceptive method chosen by the client

explanation: Following up lets you close the loop! You get to check if your client actually made it safely and got the care they needed. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T6#GNS225_U3_T6_h4)

question: Why is severe fluid in the abdomen (ascites) a big risk during a liver biopsy?

options.C: It stops numbing medicine from working on the skin

question: Which health condition can significantly delay the normal wound healing process?

options.C: Uncontrolled diabetes
options.D: Mild seasonal allergies

question: During a vaginal exam, a student midwife feels the baby's skull bones overlapping tightly with no way to separate them. How is this charted?

options.A: Grade 2 or Grade 3 moulding
options.B: Normal physiological shift
options.C: Caput succedaneum score
options.D: Grade 0 normal molding

explanation: When bones overlap firmly and won't budge, that's advanced moulding (Grade 2 or 3). It's a key sign to watch out for to prevent prolonged or blocked labour! [learn more](GNS121_U6_T14#GNS121_U6_T14_h3)

question: When choosing a speculum size for an adult patient, what should you do?

options.A: Choose the largest size that fits comfortably into the ear canal
options.B: Select a pediatric size to ensure it does not touch the eardrum
options.C: Avoid using a speculum and insert the metal otoscope head directly
options.D: Always use the smallest size available to prevent patient discomfort

explanation: A bigger speculum actually keeps you from accidentally poking the instrument in too deep, while giving you a much better view! [learn more](GNS221_U2_T3#GNS221_U2_T3_h3)

question: How does missing one fallopian tube generally affect a woman's chances of getting pregnant naturally?

options.A: The patient will instantly experience early surgical menopause
options.B: Pregnancy is still possible because the remaining tube can function
options.C: Natural conception is completely impossible without medical help
options.D: Ectopic pregnancies will occur in every single attempted cycle

explanation: Wonderful news for patients! One healthy tube is often all it takes to capture an egg and achieve a natural pregnancy. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T28#GNS216_U5_T28_h6)

question: Which muscle group forms the main support sling at the base of the pelvis?

options.A: Obturator internus
options.B: Iliopsoas
options.C: Levator ani
options.D: Rectus abdominis

explanation: You've got this! The levator ani muscles act like a sturdy muscular sling that keeps all your pelvic organs safely in place. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T12#GNS121_U5_T12_h1)

question: Which phase of disaster management involves strengthening hospital buildings so they can survive an earthquake?

options.A: Mitigation
options.B: Response
options.C: Recovery
options.D: Triage

explanation: Mitigation is all about taking action *before* a disaster strikes to reduce damage and keep people safe. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T6#GNS315_U1_T6_h4)

question: Which environmental factor constantly threatens medical electronics on a boat?

options.A: Excessive exposure to underground soil
options.B: Complete absence of magnetic fields
options.C: Saltwater corrosion and high humidity
options.D: Constant freezing temperatures indoors

explanation: Correct! The salty, humid sea air can easily rust and ruin medical devices, so nurses have to maintain equipment with extra care. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T15#GNS321_U2_T15_h5)

question: What role do cultural traditions play in nutrition?

options.A: They ensure that every person eats a balanced amount of vitamins
options.B: They prevent communities from consuming processed fast foods
options.C: They dictate the exact financial cost of groceries in a market
options.D: They dictate what foods are considered acceptable and how meals are prepared

explanation: Culture shapes food preferences, cooking methods, and the social significance attached to eating together. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T020#GNS227_U2_T020_h5)

question: What is the main danger of a massive, uncontrolled bleed?

options.A: It drops blood volume and stops oxygen flow to organs
options.B: It blocks normal clotting completely
options.C: It triggers overproduction of red blood cells
options.D: It causes an immediate spike in blood pressure

explanation: When too much blood is lost, there isn't enough volume left to pump oxygen to vital organs, which can lead to shock. Great job thinking through patient safety! [learn more](GNS221_U3_T4#GNS221_U3_T4_h1)

question: What do the blood vessels in your skin do when your body temperature gets too high and you need to cool down?

options.A: They thicken permanently
options.B: They vasodilate
options.C: They collapse entirely
options.D: They vasoconstrict

explanation: You're right! They vasodilate (open wider) to bring more warm blood close to the surface, letting excess body heat escape into the air. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T2#GNS211_U2_T2_h8)

question: Why is self-monitoring of blood glucose important for a patient managing diabetes?

options.A: It cures the underlying insulin resistance in Type 2 diabetes
options.B: It helps track daily blood sugar patterns and guide safe care
options.C: It prevents the patient from ever experiencing low blood sugar
options.D: It completely replaces the need for clinic check-ups and lab tests

explanation: Checking blood sugar at home gives immediate feedback on how food, activity, and medicine affect glucose levels day-to-day. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h3)

question: What is the primary goal of microbial identification in a clinical setting?

options.A: To count the total number of human cells in a clinical sample
options.B: To measure the patient's exact blood pressure and pulse rate
options.C: To sterilize medical equipment before a surgical procedure
options.D: To determine the exact pathogen causing an infection for targeted treatment

explanation: Knowing the specific organism allows healthcare providers to choose the most effective and narrow-spectrum treatment possible. [learn more](GST114_U5_T3#GST114_U5_T3_h1)
